v.s: A supplicant asked for a punishment bound to happen
v.c: A challenger has demanded a punishment bound to come
v.h: A Mocker Asks for Judgment Day

q: ...that will afflict the Kaafiroon, which cannot be averted...
v.s: To the disbelievers; of it there is no preventer.
v.c: for the disbelievers—to be averted by none—

q: ...and is from Allaah, the Controller of the staircase
(the skies, which the angels constantly ascend as they convey people's actions and instructions to and from Allaah).
v.s: [It is] from God, owner of the ways of ascent.
v.c: from Allah, Lord of pathways of ˹heavenly˺ ascent,

q: (This punishment that the people inquire about will take place)
the duration of which shall be
v.s: The angels and the Spirit [i.e., Gabriel] will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years.
v.c: ˹through which˺ the angels and the ˹holy˺ spirit will ascend to Him on a Day fifty thousand years in length.

q: So exercise patience in a most beautiful manner
(without complaining about the attitude of the Kuffaar and without asking for them to be punished because their punishment is imminent, either in this world or in the Aakhirah).
v.s: So be patient with gracious patience.
v.c: So endure ˹this denial, O Prophet,˺ with beautiful patience.

q: (because they do not want to believe in it)...
v.s: Indeed, they see it [as] distant,
v.c: They truly see this ˹Day˺ as impossible,

v.s: But We see it [as] near.
v.c: but We see it as inevitable.

q: The day when the sky will become
like the dirty residue of oil...
v.s: On the Day the sky will be like murky oil,
v.c: On that Day the sky will be like molten brass

q: (tossed about in the air just as flakes of wool are tossed through the air).
v.s: And the mountains will be like wool,
v.c: and the mountains like ˹tufts of˺ wool.

q: (because everyone will be worried about themselves only)...
v.s: And no friend will ask [anything of] a friend,
v.c: And no close friend will ask ˹about˺ their friends,

m: They will be made to see each other
q: ...even though they will be shown each other. The sinner will wish that as ransom for (escaping) the punishment of that day he could offer his sons...
v.s: They will be shown each other. The criminal will wish that he could be ransomed from the punishment of that Day by his children.
v.c: ˹although˺ they will be made to see each other. The wicked will wish to ransom themselves from the punishment of that Day by their children,

v.s: And his wife and his brother
v.c: their spouses, their siblings,

v.s: And his nearest kindred who shelter him.
v.c: their clan that sheltered them,

q: ...and everyone on earth so that he may be saved.
v.s: And whoever is on earth entirely [so] then it could save him.
v.c: and everyone on earth altogether, just to save themselves.

q: (No ransom will be accepted and none will be made to suffer for another.)
The Fire shall certainly be flaming...
v.s: No! Indeed, it is the Flame [of Hell],
v.c: But no! There will certainly be a raging Flame

m: of the skin of the head
q: ...(so hot that it will be capable of easily)
v.s: A remover of exteriors.
v.c: ripping off scalps.

q: will call the one who turned away
v.s: It invites he who turned his back [on truth] and went away [from obedience]
v.c: It will summon whoever turned their backs ˹on Allah˺ and turned away ˹from the truth˺,

q: who amassed wealth and tended it
(hoarded it without fulfilling the duties owed to Allaah).
v.s: And collected [wealth] and hoarded.
v.c: and gathered and hoarded ˹wealth˺.

q: Verily man has been created anxious
v.s: Indeed, mankind was created anxious:
v.c: Indeed, humankind was created impatient:

q: When difficulty afflicts him, he panics
v.s: When evil touches him, impatient,
v.c: distressed when touched with evil,

q: ...and when he experiences good fortune, he becomes miserly
(too scared to lose what he has).
v.s: And when good touches him, withholding [of it],
v.c: and withholding when touched with good—

q: (This is the condition of all people)
v.s: Except the observers of prayer -
v.c: except those who pray,

v.s: Those who are constant in their prayer
v.c: consistently performing their prayers;

v.s: And those within whose wealth is a known right
v.c: and who give the rightful share of their wealth

v.s: For the petitioner and the deprived -
v.c: to the beggar and the poor;

q: Those who believe in the truth of the day of reckoning...
v.s: And those who believe in the Day of Recompense
v.c: and who ˹firmly˺ believe in the Day of Judgment;

q: ...and who fear the punishment of their Rabb.
v.s: And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord -
v.c: and those who fear the punishment of their Lord—

q: Indeed the punishment of their Rabb is not something that one can avoid.
v.s: Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not that from which one is safe -
v.c: ˹knowing that˺ none should feel secure from their Lord’s punishment—

q: Those who guard their private parts
v.s: And those who guard their private parts
v.c: and those who guard their chastity

q: ...(who do not engage in sexual activity)
except when it comes to their spouses
and the slave women whom they own. They will surely not be blamed for
v.s: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they are not to be blamed -
v.c: except with their wives or those ˹bondwomen˺ in their possession, for then they are free from blame,

q: (which is restricted to their spouses and female slaves),
v.s: But whoever seeks beyond that, then they are the transgressors -
v.c: but whoever seeks beyond that are the transgressors.

q: (The Mu'mineen who are not like the rest of mankind are)
Those who give due regard to
v.s: And those who are to their trusts and promises attentive.
v.c: ˹The faithful are˺ also those who are true to their trusts and covenants;

q: (they do not allow anything to change their testimony)...
v.s: And those who are in their testimonies upright
v.c: and who are honest in their testimony;

q: (ensure that the time and method of performing salaah are correct and they never allow any salaah to pass by unperformed).
v.s: And those who [carefully] maintain their prayer:
v.c: and who are ˹properly˺ observant of their prayers.

q: These people shall be honoured in the gardens of Jannah.
(Eight attributes of people of Jannat have been mentioned.)
v.s: They will be in gardens, honoured.
v.c: These will be in Gardens, held in honour.

q: (Referring to the Mushrikeen who used to form several groups around Rasulullaah ﷺ near the Kabah to mock him as he recited the Qur'aan there, Allaah asks,)
What is the matter with the Kuffaar that they run towards you
v.s: So what is [the matter] with those who disbelieve, hastening [from] before you, [O Muhammad],
v.c: So what is the matter with the disbelievers that they rush ˹head-long˺ towards you ˹O Prophet˺,

q: ...in groups to your right and your left
v.s: [To sit] on [your] right and [your] left in separate groups?
v.c: from the right and the left, in groups ˹to mock you˺?

q: Does every one of them desire that he
should enter the Jannah of bliss?
v.s: Does every person among them aspire to enter a garden of pleasure?
v.c: Does every one of them expect to be admitted into a Garden of Bliss?

q: (This shall never be because only the Mu'mineen shall enter Jannah regardless of their social standing in this world)
Verily We have created them from what they know.
(When man knows that Allaah has created him from something as insignificant as a drop of semen, how can he question Allaah's ability to resurrect him on the Day of Qiyaamah?)
v.s: No! Indeed, We have created them from that which they know.
v.c: But no! Indeed, they ˹already˺ know what We created them from.

q: I swear by the Rabb of the Easts
v.s: So I swear by the Lord of [all] risings and settings that indeed We are able
v.c: So, I do swear by the Lord of ˹all˺ the points of sunrise and sunset that We are truly capable

q: to substitute them with people better than them. We certainly have the power
(to do this and anything else We wish to do).
v.s: To replace them with better than them; and We are not to be outdone.
v.c: of replacing them with ˹others˺ better than them, and We cannot be prevented ˹from doing so˺.

q: (if the Kuffaar refuse to accept Islaam after you have done your best to convince them, then)
until they meet their day that they are promised...
v.s: So leave them to converse vainly and amuse themselves until they meet their Day which they are promised -
v.c: So let them indulge ˹in falsehood˺ and amuse ˹themselves˺ until they face their Day, which they have been threatened with—

q: when they will hurriedly emerge from the graves as if they are rushing towards a temple
v.s: The Day they will emerge from the graves rapidly as if they were, toward an erected idol, hastening.
v.c: the Day they will come forth from the graves swiftly, as if racing to an idol ˹for a blessing˺,

q: will surround them. This is the day that they had been promised
v.s: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. That is the Day which they had been promised.
v.c: with eyes downcast, utterly covered with disgrace. That is the Day they have ˹always˺ been warned of.
